stories.headline: PSD-AUR no-confidence motion topples Bolojan's pro-EU government in 281-4 vote
stories.summary: On May 5, Romanian parliament passed a no-confidence motion 281-4, removing Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan after PSD withdrew from the coalition in late April and joined with far-right AUR to file the motion. The collapse drew widespread international coverage as the first time in post-communist Romania that a nominally pro-European party allied with far-right euroskeptics to bring down a government, with analysts warning about the risk to Romania's EU budget-deficit commitments and credit ratings.

stories.headline: Post-collapse coalition negotiations: PNL-USR form opposition bloc, PSD seeks new government
stories.summary: Following the government collapse, President Nicușor Dan began informal consultations with party leaders at Cotroceni to form a new government. PSD insisted on a new broad coalition but without Bolojan as PM; PNL formally voted to refuse any new coalition with PSD (50-4 in its leadership body), and PNL and USR announced a joint opposition front. PSD expressed confidence a new majority could be assembled within 10 days.

stories.headline: PNL internal split over coalition stance: Predoiu rebels, Bogdan dismisses breakaway fears
stories.summary: Following PNL's formal vote to enter opposition, a pro-PSD faction within the party led by figures including Cătălin Predoiu attempted to reverse the decision. Reports emerged of plans to split PNL and form a new parliamentary group aligned with PSD. Senior PNL European Parliament member Rareș Bogdan publicly dismissed fears of a party split, while local mayors remain divided between loyalty to Bolojan and the need for government funding.

stories.headline: AUR claims future governing role, presents 10-point administrative reform plan
stories.summary: AUR leader George Simion declared that his party 'assumes' a future governing role following the government collapse, while stating he does not wish to govern with either PSD or PNL. AUR presented a 10-point plan for administrative reform including cutting administrative spending by 1% of GDP annually, reducing parliament to 300 members, and limiting the government to 10 ministries. Simion also filed a complaint with the People's Advocate over the caretaker government issuing Emergency Ordinance 38/2026.

stories.headline: S&P Global warns of Romania credit rating downgrade amid fiscal and political risks
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings issued downgrade warnings for Romania's sovereign credit rating, citing the government collapse as a potential complicating factor for 2027 budget discussions and Romania's commitment to narrowing its EU-record budget deficit. Interim Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare held calls with Fitch and Moody's, stating the fiscal trajectory for 2026 remained unchanged despite the political crisis.

stories.headline: Romanian leu hits record lows against euro; BNR intervenes, reserves fall €2.2 billion
stories.summary: The leu fell to successive record lows against the euro in the days surrounding the no-confidence vote, reaching 5.27 lei/euro before recovering slightly to 5.2364 by May 8. BNR spent approximately €2.2 billion in April defending the currency, reducing foreign reserves to €64.8 billion. BNR spokesperson Dan Suciu stated market calm depended on political and fiscal stability rather than central bank action. Bloomberg reported the crisis was testing BNR's managed-float regime.
